challenge_statement: Irreversibility under Axiom 3.3 must forbid numerical identity restoration after lawful death.
forbidden_shortcuts: No numerically identical restoration after lawful death is allowed without an explicit theorem.
formal_argument_body: The irreversibility claim stands or falls on the corollary route from Axiom 3.3 rather than on rhetoric about finality.

If lawful death has occurred, any later state that is merely structurally similar must be classified separately; it may not be counted as the same realized identity without contradicting the corollary.
This dossier therefore treats numerical identity restoration as a falsifier rather than as an interpretive option.
The dossier is now locked as a passed formal review under the exact source route and may be reopened only by a surviving falsifier.
falsifier_conditions: Construct a lawful death event followed by numerically identical restoration of the same continuum.
Show that the current corollary route requires hidden premises to exclude restoration.
exit_criterion: The irreversibility corollary is formalized as a dossier with explicit counterexample conditions and no identity loophole.
